title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Lunaris Analytics - Cost/Econ Review
summary: Weekly POC sync to review cost/unit economics from last week's benchmarks. Discussed tokens/sec per dollar, caching savings from prefix/KV cache, batching vs latency tradeoffs, and quantization profiles. Agreed to run focused end-to-end benchmark with larger batch sizes and KV warm cache; Redwood to share updated cost model and revised runbook.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-23 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Ari, Maya (Redwood) / Jordan, Sasha, Priya, Evan (Lunaris)

[00:00] Ari: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — agenda is cost econ review, run through the spreadsheet, look at cache numbers and batching tradeoffs, and next steps. Maya's going to lead the benchmark discussion.
[00:22] Maya: hi all, I'll share screen in a sec, but quick TL;DR: baseline hosted run last week gave us about 720 tokens/sec on the 32-token context profile, cost came in around $0.95 per thousand tokens using the default q4 profile; with prefix caching warmed we saw effective tokens/sec/$ jump to approx 1,800 tokens/sec per $1 — that's the tokens per second per dollar equivalent we calculated.
[01:05] Jordan: sorry can you repeat the tokens/sec/$ number? we want to make sure our PMs see the delta.
[01:12] Maya: yeah so raw throughput was ~720 t/s on the un-cached path; cost model using usage rates in the sheet gives ~560k tokens per dollar per hour, converting that to a steady tokens/sec per dollar number we get ~1,800 tokens/sec per $1 when cache hits are happening for repeated prefixes. When cache is cold it's more like 450 t/s per $1.
[01:40] Priya: that's a big swing. are those cache hits realistic for our ecom chat flows? we have high prefix reuse for product descriptions but not always for free-text questions.
[01:52] Evan: right our distribution is mixed; about 35% of queries hit the same product prompts, but long-tail questions vary. we care about p99 latency as product needs sub-300ms for UI.
[02:10] Maya: noted. the warm-cache numbers assume our prefix cache does 60-70% hit rate for the specific paths; for p99 we saw median 120ms but p99 rose to 520ms without batching limits. Using smaller max-batch-size (4) keeps p99 under 300ms but reduces throughput and tokens/sec per $ by about 20-30%.
[03:01] Sasha: can you explain the batching tradeoff again? we thought increasing batch size always improved tokens/sec/$, but we hit the p99 latency SLO.
[03:10] Maya: yep so with continuous batching you amortize kernel overhead and improve GPU utilization — that raises tokens/sec/$ because more tokens are processed per GPU-second. But bigger batches mean requests wait to fill the batch, which increases tail latency. For our workload, a batch size of 8 gave best cost efficiency (tokens/sec/$ improved ~35%) but p99 was ~480ms; batch size of 2 had p99 ~260ms but cost efficiency dropped ~22%.
[03:48] Jordan: what's the recommendation for hosted vs dedicated given this? We might need predictable p99 for UI.
[03:56] Ari: two levers: dedicated instances with reserved pools lower variability and allow tighter batching policies (e.g., accelerated micro-batching) and you can pin quantized model variants. Hosted can be tuned but you'll see more inter-tenant variance. If p99 is a hard SLO, Dedicated with an autoscaling buffer is recommended.
[04:20] Priya: cost delta roughly? we need a ballpark to present to finance.
[04:24] Maya: rough back-of-envelope: hosted at current usage profile is about $X — sorry I'll pull numbers from the sheet — (shares link) https://redwood.example/benchmarks/lunaris-poc. For Dedicated, if you commit to a monthly pool (example: 4x A10s equivalent) you'd see per-token unit cost drop ~30-40% compared to peak hosted. But there's fixed commit cost. For our smaller pilot it may not be justified until QPS doubles.
[05:05] Evan: you mentioned quantization profiles. what's the quality impact for our summarization tests?
[05:12] Maya: we ran q4->q8 and bfloat mixes. q8b gave best perf for cost (tokens/sec/$ up ~15%) with negligible ROUGE/QA drift on your eval set; q4 looked slightly cheaper but we saw a few regression cases in long-context summarization — some hallucination increase. We recommend q8b for production-like.
[05:40] Jordan: can you remind me what KV cache vs prefix cache buys us? we have both in architecture.
[05:44] Maya: prefix cache stores encoder/decoder outputs for repeated initial prompts; KV cache stores key/value states for the decoder and speeds up autoregressive decoding on subsequent tokens — for chat with repeated system messages, prefix cache gives biggest reduction in compute per request, whereas KV warms help on long responses. In your workload prefix caching was the bigger win because of repeated product prompt templates.
[06:10] Priya: in the raw bench we saw 38% token reduction attributed to prefix reuse — does that align?
[06:15] Maya: yes, that matches our instrumentation. With 60% prefix hit rate and KV warm we modeled effective token compute drop of ~40%, translating to the tokens/sec/$ uplift I mentioned.
[06:26] Sasha: from infra perspective, do we need a VPC or any special networking for Dedicated? also curious about KMS for PII logs.
[06:35] Ari: Private / Dedicated supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS/HSM. For pilot you can use hosted and turn on customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest. For Dedicated we'd set up a private control plane.
[06:50] Jordan: what's the expected time to run the end-to-end benchmark you suggested last time? we want numbers that match our real traffic pattern (mixture of short prompts, long summaries).
[06:57] Maya: we propose a 48-hour run with traffic replay using your sampled distribution; that'll give stable tokens/sec and cost numbers across diurnal patterns. We can run a 6-hour smoke first.
[07:10] Priya: can Redwood run the smoke and share logs so we can validate p99?
[07:15] Ari: yes we'll run smoke and share the raw traces and the benchmark sheet.
[07:20] Maya: a couple of notes from the spreadsheet: 1) We included a tokens/sec per $ calculation column — note it's sensitive to batch and cache assumptions; 2) We added a column for effective latency under X% cache hit rates so you can see p95/p99 change.
[07:42] Evan: one more ask — can we see the microbenchmark on gpus with perf counters? we'd like kernel-level numbers to compare to our on-prem baseline.
[07:50] Maya: yes we can provide per-kernel breakdown for the quantized run; we'll need to run it on the specific instance type you care about.
[08:00] Jordan: ok recap please — what are the concrete next steps and owners?
[08:06] Ari: sure. recap: (1) Redwood to run 6-hour smoke replay next 48h and share traces/sheet; (2) Redwood to run quantized q8b end-to-end benchmark on the A10-equivalent for 48h and include per-kernel breakdown; (3) Lunaris to provide final traffic sample and confirm cache-hit assumptions by 2026-03-25; (4) decide by next week if Dedicated commit is worth pursuing.
[08:35] Priya: timeline works. any outstanding blockers? security docs?
[08:38] Ari: we'll send SOC2 docs and KMS integration guide; Maya will share a short runbook for cache warm strategies.
[08:46] Jordan: great thanks everyone.

[09:00] End meeting.
